title: Colorado Springs' Indian Food Festival Returns for Fourth Year on Aug. 1
excerpt: The free, family-friendly event at Liberty High School will feature a dozen Indian food vendors, cultural performances, dandiya dance lessons, and a fashion show, with 30% of proceeds going to charity.
body:
• The fourth annual Indian Food Festival takes place Aug. 1, from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., at Liberty High School in Colorado Springs, with free general admission starting at noon.
  • Around a dozen Indian restaurants and food vendors from Colorado Springs and Denver will serve dishes ranging from biryanis and curries to dosas, idli, and street food.
  • Cultural programming includes dandiya dance lessons, Bollywood performances, free henna, and an Indian fashion show.
  • Thirty percent of all proceeds will be donated to the Hindu University of America (HUA).

The annual Indian Food Festival will return to Colorado Springs on Saturday, Aug. 1, marking the event's fourth year of bringing Indian cuisine, music, and cultural programming to the Pikes Peak region, according to FOX21 News Colorado.

The festival runs from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. at Liberty High School, 8720 Scarborough Drive. General admission is free starting at noon, though registration through Eventbrite is required. An early-access pass, priced at $13, grants entry at 11 a.m. with reserved seating, raffle entry, and a swag bag.

A Growing Celebration of Indian Cuisine

Organized by Monika Celly through Polka Dots and Curry, the festival has steadily expanded since its debut as the Indian Harvest Festival in January 2024. That first event drew visitors to the same Liberty High School gymnasium, which organizers transformed into what they described as "a beautiful mini India with vibrant booths and a stage full of hustle and bustle."

This year's food lineup features roughly a dozen Indian restaurants, chefs, and food carts from both Colorado Springs and Denver. Visitors can expect dishes spanning India's regional diversity — aromatic biryanis, fragrant curries, crispy samosas, South Indian staples like dosas, idli, vada, and sambhar, along with street food, desserts, and beverages including lassi, masala chai, and spiced lemonade.

Non-food vendors selling clothing, jewelry, home décor, and wellness products will also have stalls at the festival.

Cultural Programming and Performances

Beyond the food, the event features a full slate of cultural activities. Attendees can take free dandiya dance lessons — the traditional stick dance from Gujarat — offered every 60 minutes throughout the day. Local community members will perform traditional and Bollywood dances on the gymnasium stage, and a free mehndi (henna) station will operate while supplies last.

An Indian fashion show, introduced at a previous edition, will return this year, showcasing traditional Indian attire alongside contemporary designs.

"We're curating a vibrant mix of food, culture, and shopping for the Indian Food Festival."

— Indian Food Festival Colorado organizers

Charitable Mission

Thirty percent of all proceeds from the event will go to HUA, the Hindu University of America, an accredited institution focused on Hindu studies. The festival has maintained this charitable component since its early editions, channeling a significant share of vendor and ticket revenue to causes aligned with the Indian-American community.

Sponsors have included local Colorado Springs businesses and tech organizations. Dev2Next, a developer conference based in Colorado Springs, backed last year's edition.

Colorado's Growing Indian Cultural Scene

The festival is one of several events connecting the Indian diaspora in Colorado. The Indian Community of Colorado Springs, a separate nonprofit, hosts its own annual charity show, Lok Kala, which has raised funds for organizations including the Morgan Adams Foundation, CASA, and the Colorado Springs Police and Fire Departments.

Colorado Springs magazine Springsmag listed the Indian Food Festival among the city's best summer festivals for 2026, writing that visitors can "celebrate India's rich culinary heritage, from the streets of New Delhi to the coastal kitchens of Kerala."

For Indian Americans in the region, the festival offers a rare concentrated gathering of regional Indian food in a state where the cuisine's presence has traditionally centered on the Front Range corridor closer to Denver.

What to Know Before You Go

The festival takes place entirely indoors in the Liberty High School gymnasium. Free parking is available onsite across four lots. Last call for food purchases is 3:30 p.m., and the reception desk closes at that time.

Registration is required for all attendees, including those with free general admission tickets. Passes can be obtained through Eventbrite, and early-access tickets are available while supplies last. For vendor or sponsorship inquiries, organizers can be reached at coloradoindianfoodfest@gmail.com or through indianfoodfestival.co.
